policy: An explicit citation, an analogous ethical structure, a proposed genealogy and a modern application are different relations. None establishes a private belief, motive or entire historical chain solely by resemblance.

comparisons.title: Luke's afterlife narrative directs its hearers to Moses
comparisons.to: Moses and the prophets as an already available obligation
comparisons.finding: The story's conclusion explicitly directs the living to the inherited texts rather than requiring a new messenger from the dead.
comparisons.inference: The author reads future judgment as exposing failure to meet an existing obligation, not replacing concern for present suffering.
comparisons.limit: This is a literary and theological reading; it cannot recover what a historical Moses would have thought of Jesus.

comparisons.title: Mark's resurrection argument invokes the book of Moses
comparisons.to: Exodus 3 and the divine relationship with the ancestors
comparisons.finding: Jesus is portrayed arguing through the burning-bush account.
comparisons.inference: A later claim can be advanced as an interpretation of inherited covenantal commitments.
comparisons.limit: An interpretive appeal is not proof that the cited passage originally made every later doctrinal claim explicit.

comparisons.title: The den-of-robbers charge has a prophetic context
comparisons.finding: The Temple protest uses language from a warning against treating sanctuary as protection while wronging others.
comparisons.inference: The author's parallel concerns an institution's obligation to the standard it claims to serve.
comparisons.limit: Neither passage is an audit proving every exchange transaction fraudulent or every priest identical.

comparisons.title: Seven-year release is not identical to Jubilee
comparisons.finding: The passages distinguish timing, debt, land, service and protected populations, and include exceptions.
comparisons.inference: Restraints on dependence can inform the author's ethical comparison without inventing a universal ancient abolition program.
comparisons.limit: Stated rules are not proof of uniform enforcement. Foreign slavery in Leviticus 25:44-46 must remain visible.

comparisons.title: An Egyptian funerary inscription joins generosity and an enduring future
comparisons.to: The proposed moral relationship between resources, care and posthumous welfare
comparisons.finding: The museum's inscription translation connects aid to known and unknown recipients with endurance on earth and welfare in the necropolis.
comparisons.inference: Egypt provides a positive ethical comparison, not only a target against which later ethics must be defined.
comparisons.limit: A self-presentation is not a verified record of every deed. The stela does not supply a complete transmission route to Jesus.

comparisons.title: Aaron's image, Moses's response and the Levites' action
comparisons.finding: The narrative distinguishes making the calf from destroying it; its announced festival names Yahweh.
comparisons.inference: Study representation and cultic continuity without attributing the image's introduction to Moses.
comparisons.limit: The narrative's violence must not be omitted. Its gold object is not an explicit economic manifesto about accumulation.

comparisons.title: Midianite connections do not narrate an established collective amnesia
comparisons.finding: The texts place Moses in Midian and narrate divine disclosure and Jethro's later response; the scholarly abstract proposes several supporting evidential strands.
comparisons.inference: A transmission inquiry can remain open without inventing an explicit story that the Levites forgot and relearned the name.
comparisons.limit: The full restricted article was not read. Divine-name traditions do not independently establish an afterlife belief.

comparisons.title: Sheol and embalming occur within the Torah
comparisons.to: The supplied claim of complete Torah silence about death
comparisons.finding: Jacob refers to Sheol, and the narrative depicts Jacob's and Joseph's embalming without explicit condemnation of those acts.
comparisons.inference: A practical emphasis on life and land is compatible with some language about the dead.
comparisons.limit: Neither example proves a complete later heaven-and-hell system, or every belief held by a historical Moses.

comparisons.title: Josephus's Hyksos association is a witness, not a settled date
comparisons.from: Against Apion 1, reporting and interpreting Manetho
comparisons.finding: An ancient author connects the departure story with the history of his people.
comparisons.inference: Investigate whether memory, reinterpretation or a historical event underlies the connection.
comparisons.limit: The mediated account does not identify a contemporary document naming Moses or prove every detail of the Exodus narrative.

comparisons.title: Sadducees, Pharisees and sons of darkness are not one economic label
comparisons.from: Josephus's sect descriptions and the War Scroll excerpt
comparisons.to: The proposed archetype of wealth-based exemption
comparisons.finding: The sources distinguish doctrines and adversaries rather than defining all opponents by the possession of wealth.
comparisons.inference: Apply a critique to a documented practice, not to an entire religious or ethnic population.
comparisons.limit: Ancient authors' generalizations also need contextual interpretation; they are not interviews establishing every member's motives.

comparisons.title: Wealth as a master is distinct from an attested pagan deity
comparisons.to: The author's God of Gold metaphor
comparisons.finding: Wealth can be criticized as misplaced reliance while a separate Christian text directs its use toward generosity.
comparisons.inference: The moral test concerns what resources serve and whom their use benefits or harms.
comparisons.limit: The metaphor is not proof of an ancient named cult or a diagnosis of every wealthy person.

comparisons.title: Private survival versus refusal of shared responsibility
comparisons.from: The proposed comparison with shelters, longevity research and space projects
comparisons.to: Documented access, labor, public costs and externalized risk
comparisons.finding: No newly investigated present-day individual or project is identified in this edition.
comparisons.inference: A project fits the proposed criticism only insofar as evidence connects privileged protection with harms or obligations shifted onto others.
comparisons.limit: Safety, medical progress and long-term planning are not themselves proof of exploitation. Beneficial shared effects would count against an unqualified condemnation.
